item.title: Future of Space Nuclear Power Symposium Scheduled in D.C.
item.description:
According to NIST Manufacturing:
The inaugural Future of Space Nuclear Power Symposium will convene in Washington, D.C., bringing together engineers, developers, industry representatives, and government leaders. Co-hosted by the American Nuclear Society, NIST, and the Office of Space Commerce, the event addresses practical requirements for developing and scaling space nuclear systems.
Discussions will center on power and propulsion technologies, operational needs for orbital and lunar surface missions, and the establishment of industry standards. The symposium aims to unite commercial enterprises, nuclear laboratories, and policymakers to drive rapid innovation in space nuclear activities.

item.title: NIST to Host Second Semiconductor Traceability and Provenance Workshop
item.description:
According to NIST Manufacturing:
The semiconductor supply chain is notoriously complex, spanning design, fabrication, assembly, and deployment across the globe. To ensure products are authentic and secure, NIST is collaborating with industry leaders, government agencies, and academia to build standardized frameworks for tracking chips.
Building upon previous workshops held in 2024, 2025, and early 2026, the upcoming December 8 workshop moves past identifying high-level needs into actionable implementation. Participants will pinpoint specific data elements, artifacts, and concepts needed to establish reliable provenance without compromising sensitive proprietary information.

item.title: Coherus cuts 30% of workforce to focus on esophageal cancer drug trials
item.description:
Coherus Oncology announced a 30% reduction in its workforce as the company scales back its broader cancer pipeline to focus specifically on esophageal indications for its investigational combination therapy.
Last month, Coherus reported phase 1b data for the combination of tagmokitug, a CCR8-targeting antibody, and its approved PD-1 blocker Loqtorzi. According to the company, the combination demonstrated a confirmed overall response rate of 75% in front-line esophageal squamous cell carcinoma patients, regardless of PD-L1 status. Chief Medical Officer Rosh Dias stated that the data suggest regulatory T cells are a critical driver of resistance, and that tagmokitug enhances PD-1 activity.
To align with this narrowed strategy, Chief Financial Officer Bryan McMichael reported that the workforce reduction and pipeline narrowing will lower core cash burn by $6 million to $7 million quarterly over the next two quarters. The company reported third-quarter revenue of $14 million for Loqtorzi, its FDA-approved treatment for nasopharyngeal carcinoma, and ended September with $83.6 million in cash. Coherus plans to maintain selected other trials, including a phase 1b study with Johnson & Johnson and an ongoing phase 2 trial in liver cancer, while aiming for financial self-sufficiency.

item.title: AbCellera drops its OX40 drug program following industry-wide setbacks
item.description: Background AbCellera was developing ABCL575, an antibody targeting the OX40 ligand intended to treat atopic dermatitis and other autoimmune conditions. While its phase 1 trial successfully met tolerability and pharmacokinetic goals, the company decided not to advance the candidate past this initial stage, citing external developments across the entire OX40 drug class. Industry Context The broader OX40 class has faced significant hurdles recently. Earlier in the year, Kyowa Kirin and Amgen halted clinical studies for rocatinlimab due to emerging malignancy concerns. Subsequently, Sanofi scrapped regulatory submission plans for amlitelimab, conceding it offered no meaningful therapeutic improvement despite originating from an expensive $1.1 billion acquisition. Conversely, some developers like Inhibrx Biosciences remain optimistic, reporting positive early results for cancer immunotherapy combinations. Pipeline Shift With the OX40 program shelved, AbCellera is shifting its internal focus toward other pipeline assets. Its lead candidate is now ABCL635, an NK3 receptor-targeting antibody for menopausal hot flashes, which recently achieved a phase 2 success and is positioned as a potential non-hormonal therapy competing with existing commercial options.

item.title: Experts fear Treasury's proposed China biotech investment ban will backfire on U.S. leadership
item.description: The Proposed Rules and Industry Anxiety The U.S. Department of the Treasury released a 163-page draft policy detailing how it plans to implement the COINS Act, which seeks to add pharmaceutical compounds to an outbound investment blacklist. While traditional cash-based licensing deals remain untouched, the proposal places ambiguous restrictions on equity investments, co-development deals, and joint ventures involving Chinese entities, leaving biopharma executives and trade attorneys struggling to define compliant behavior. The Threat of a 'Flying Blind' Strategy Industry heavyweights, including a coalition of prominent healthcare investors led by RA Capital, argue that the rules will backfire. By barring U.S. investors and drugmakers from engaging in equity and co-commercialization structures in China, American firms will lose vital visibility into the global clinical pipeline. Critics warn that European investors and multinational pharmaceutical companies—unbound by these strict rules—will scoop up promising Chinese assets, leaving U.S. players at a severe disadvantage. The 'Joint Venture' Riddle and Economic Security A major source of confusion is the Treasury's lack of a clear legal definition for 'joint ventures,' which threatens popular models like U.S.-based 'NewCos' formed around Chinese-licensed assets. Legal experts note that the broad scope reflects a shifting political reality where economic security is treated as national security. Although the industry is pushing for narrower definitions focused strictly on bioweapons or select agents, analysts suggest that policymakers are determined to protect U.S. technological leadership across the board, regardless of the compliance burden and potential chilling effect on cross-border R&D.

item.title: Production MLOps at GS Caltex with Amazon SageMaker Canvas
item.description:
According to AWS Machine Learning:
GS Caltex, a South Korean energy and chemical company, divides AI model development between process engineers and machine learning engineers. Process engineers build and validate models visually in Amazon SageMaker Canvas without writing code. Meanwhile, ML engineers configure Amazon SageMaker Pipelines for deployment and scheduled inference.
To bridge the gap between development and production, GS Caltex automated the handoff process. ML engineers previously spent about a week on integration tasks like setting data paths and connecting preprocessing jobs. With the new automated setup, they can deploy models within a few hours. The company now runs batch inference every 30 minutes, which eliminates the need to keep costly real-time prediction endpoints running continuously and lowers overall costs.

item.title: Google Research releases Antigravity teamwork and Gemini 4 for scientific problem solving
item.description: According to Google Research: Background and Design Google Research details the design and applications of Antigravity's teamwork multiagent systems, built on top of various Gemini models including Gemini 4 Argon, Carbon, and Hydrogen. Frontier research requires navigating vast literature, building computational pipelines, and verifying every step. To address the unreliability of single model generations and the loss of context in multi-day tasks, teamwork uses parallel exploration paired with dedicated falsifiers like Lean 4 proof checkers and execution simulators, while partitioning context across specialized agents. Scientific and Engineering Results According to Google, teams across Google and academic institutions used these multi-agent workflows to solve long-standing open problems. In mathematics and theoretical computer science, researchers proved the 2013 Courtade–Kumar conjecture, resolved a 2014 open question in adaptive data analysis, and formalized complex proofs in Lean 4, including the Weil conjectures and parts of the Navier–Stokes equations. In systems software and hardware engineering, the tools were used to build the FarArray low-latency kernel-bypass system, rewrite large codebases like the Zircon microkernel and libgav1 into safe Rust, and optimize TPU kernels, yielding significant performance gains over manual implementations. Availability Google states that these features, along with the /boost command and Deep Review document evaluation tools, are currently available in Antigravity. Additionally, Google has opened applications providing 10,000 academic researchers with six months of free access to their highest usage tier.

item.title: ChatGPT Wallet lets OpenAI's Dots agents buy things for you
item.description: Background and Rollout OpenAI is expanding its Dots AI agents platform, introduced earlier this year, by adding a dedicated payment tool called ChatGPT Wallet. The feature is rolling out to ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US who are 18 and older, requiring a US billing address and eligible major credit cards from American Express, Chase, Mastercard, and Visa. Security and Privacy OpenAI reports that users must add a card to the wallet, after which Dots agents can initiate purchases based on user prompts. However, the agent must check in with the user before finalizing any transaction. Every purchase requires a security check using biometric verification, such as Face ID or a fingerprint scan. Similar to Apple Pay or Google Wallet, the system replaces actual credit card details with a payment token, meaning card numbers are hidden from both the AI agent and the merchant. Future Plans and Limitations Looking ahead, OpenAI expects users to eventually fully delegate purchases to their agents by defining parameters like spending limits, approved categories, or specific timeframes. However, practical hurdles remain. Some retailers restrict or block AI agents entirely, similar to how Amazon blocked Meta's Muse agents earlier this year. OpenAI notes that online stores must update their websites, payment gateways, and risk systems to accommodate legitimate agent purchases and prevent accidental blocking.

item.title: Build a Robot Pick-and-Place Simulation with SimReady Assets
item.description:
The walkthrough outlines a step-by-step process for building a beverage can pick-and-place simulation using the UR17G arm, Robotiq 2F-140 gripper, and a soda can within Isaac Sim 6.2. According to the text, SimReady Central provides OpenUSD assets equipped with pre-defined simulation properties such as collisions, mass, and joint settings, validated against specific profiles like Robot-Body and Robot-Gripper.
Developers can rely on AI agents combined with Isaac Sim skills to automate tasks, including loading local USD files, inspecting joint limits, assembling the arm and gripper into a single articulation, and generating Python-based movement controls. The guide emphasizes pre-run behavior checks—such as verifying joint settings, testing small arm movements, and confirming that objects rest correctly on work surfaces without falling through—to ensure the virtual robot interacts accurately with its environment.

item.title: IEEE Spectrum Video Friday Highlights NASA's PROMISE Moon Rover and In-Space Assembly
item.description: This week's IEEE Spectrum robotics video compilation highlights several developments across space and terrestrial robotics. According to the report, NASA plans to send a nuclear-powered rover named PROMISE to the Moon's South Pole, utilizing spare and test-bed hardware from previous Mars missions. In space manufacturing, a Caltech payload under DARPA's NOM4D program successfully assembled a truss structure in orbit using a gantry robot and a reflective mesh. Terrestrially, Boston Dynamics tested a wheeled version of its Atlas humanoid, while Corvus Robotics showcased autonomous inventory drones operating without localized infrastructure at an ASICS distribution center.

item.title: langchain-openai==1.8.0 - Dropping Python 3.10 Support and Adding OpenAIClassifier
item.description:
Version Update Details
The langchain-openai maintainers announce the release of version 1.8.0, which includes several key updates for developers building applications with language models. The most notable change is that Python 3.10 support has been dropped because it reached its end-of-life, making Python 3.11 the new minimum requirement. Users staying on older Python environments will automatically stick with the 1.7.x branch. New Features and Improvements
Beyond environment adjustments, this release introduces the OpenAIClassifier designed for the Generally Available Decisions API. Additionally, the team refreshed internal model profile data to ensure better compatibility and performance with recent updates.

item.title: LangChain Raises $300M Series C at $3B Valuation
item.description:
According to LangChain Blog:
LangChain announced that it has raised $300 million in Series C funding at a valuation of $3 billion, led by CapitalG with participation from GIC, DFJ Growth, IVP, and Sapphire Ventures. The company believes that AI agents will transform the economy, and every enterprise will need to control its own intelligence, data, and infrastructure to build competitive advantages.
To capture this market, LangChain highlights its LangSmith platform, which serves over 7,000 organizations—including Fortune 500 enterprises like NVIDIA and Toyota as well as startups like Harvey. LangSmith is structured around three core pillars: Agent Runtime (infrastructure and architecture for running agents), Agent Improvement (testing, monitoring, and automated optimization), and Agent Governance (centralized control over models, tools, and sensitive data). The company also announced an upcoming release event scheduled for Friday, November 20th, to introduce new platform capabilities.

item.title: HHS pumps up to $25M into ibogaine, other psychotropic drugs on Veteran’s Day
item.description:
The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services announced up to $25 million in investments targeting psychotropic compounds, with a particular focus on the psychedelic substance ibogaine. ARPA-H is allocating up to $4.9 million over five years for investigational medicines addressing PTSD, with subsequent awards slated for substance use disorders. Meanwhile, the National Institute of Mental Health is launching a $20 million funding opportunity for a research network examining treatments like ketamine, psilocybin, and esketamine.
Ibogaine has been a central focus of the Trump administration, supported by an executive order in April aimed at accelerating psychedelic therapies. Researchers note that ibogaine operates through a complex matrix pharmacology rather than a single target. While proponents highlight promising anecdotal and preliminary findings, the compound is also associated with neurotoxic and cardiotoxic risks, with published literature recording 33 deaths following its use as of 2022.

item.title: Release v5.23.0 - New Model Additions and Exporters Update
item.description:
New Model Additions
This release adds support for several prominent model families. Inkling2 is a multi-modal model supporting text and image inputs with a large parameter scale. Liquid AI's LFM3 and LFM3-VL introduce hybrid architectures combining gated short convolutions and grouped-query attention. Other notable additions include IQuestCoder for code generation, Shanghai AI Laboratory's InternLM3 instruction-tuned model, and experimental decision heads like JEV. Exporters and Backend Runtimes
The update brings a major overhaul to model exports. Every export now returns an ExportedModel, which shares the same API as the original model and can be pushed to the Hub and reloaded. It supports Dynamo, ONNX Runtime, OpenVINO, and ExecuTorch, with built-in runtime fusions that make decoding significantly faster than standard PyTorch eager execution. Core Bugfixes and Optimizations
Beyond new models, version 5.23.0 addresses a wide range of issues across vision pipelines, distributed training, attention mechanisms, caching, and audio processing. These include fixing cache correctness in various models, optimizing expert parallelism, and improving overall stability for multi-GPU setups.

item.title: 5 food and beverage companies making sustainable packaging changes
item.description:
Food and beverage manufacturers are facing mounting pressure from new extended producer responsibility laws and shifting consumer preferences, leading to practical updates in product packaging.
Several major brands have recently implemented specific material swaps. Campbell's replaced plastic dog bone packaging with a recyclable paper clip for Rao's sauce jars, removed mixed-material layers in its plastic bottles, and added recycled content to its pretzel canisters. PepsiCo reduced its overall plastic use by over 7 million pounds by lightweighting Gatorade and Lipton bottles. Target eliminated carbon-black colorant from its bakery and deli trays to make them more compatible with existing recycling systems. Bel Group swapped the outer cellophane wrap of Babybel cheese for paper to save an estimated 850 metric tons of packaging material annually globally. Meanwhile, Mars partnered with Berry Global to transition large M&M's, Skittles, and Starburst pantry jars to 100 percent post-consumer recycled plastic, aiming to eliminate over 1,300 metric tons of virgin plastic each year.

item.title: llama.cpp reaches v1.0.0, establishing a stable API for local AI development
item.description:
After three and a half years of growth, the llama.cpp project has become a foundational tool for running multi-modal large language models locally on everything from consumer computers to enterprise servers. With the release of version 1.0.0 for both llama.cpp and its tensor library ggml, the team aims to provide a more reliable foundation for the expanding ecosystem of local AI applications.
To support this growth, the project is establishing strict semantic versioning rules. Any breaking changes to the public C application programming interface will now trigger major version bumps, making interface boundaries clearer for developers who integrate the software into their products. Additionally, the project continues to expand its distribution channels and hardware support, utilizing infrastructure from Hugging Face alongside hardware partnerships with major chipmakers to ensure code quality and broad platform compatibility.

item.title: Marea Touts Phase 2 Lipid Disorder Win for MAR001
item.description: Clinical Results Cardiometabolic biotech Marea Therapeutics, now a subsidiary of Lisata Therapeutics following a September acquisition, released data from the first part of a phase 2b study evaluating its drug candidate MAR001. According to the company, the angiopoietin-like protein 4 (ANGPTL4)-targeting monoclonal antibody reduced triglycerides by 72.2% in patients with levels at or above 500 mg/dL, and by 57.2% in those at or above 300 mg/dL. More than half of the 235 adult patients on MAR001 reached normal triglyceride levels, compared to 3.4% on placebo. Treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 69.5% of MAR001-treated patients, slightly below the 77.6% rate for the placebo cohort. Pipeline and Future Plans Marea CEO Josh Lehrer stated in an interview that the data is encouraging for establishing an optimal treatment for patients facing the dual threat of pancreatitis and cardiovascular risk. The company has already initiated the second part of the mid-stage study involving 100 patients, and plans to take a half-life-extended version called MAR005 into a phase 3 study for severe hypertriglyceridemia. Additionally, Marea is exploring the potential for its pipeline to address obesity and has a candidate named MAR002 in early-stage trials for acromegaly. Background The acquisition of Marea followed Lisata's failed deal with Kuva Labs, which resulted in significant workforce reductions. The subsequent merger with Marea involved a stock-for-stock transaction backed by a $225 million commitment from investors including Forbion, venBio, and Third Rock Ventures.

item.title: Delix raises $100M for depression drug without psychedelic trips
item.description: Background Delix Therapeutics, a Boston-based biotech born from a University of California lab in 2019, focuses on developing neuroplastogens, a class of drugs aimed at regrowing lost brain connections without causing traditional psychedelic trips. Details The newly raised $100 million Series C round was led by J&J's venture arm, with participation from several other investors. The funds will primarily advance its lead oral candidate, zalsupindole, which is based on a naturally occurring compound found in plants and toad secretions. Delix reported positive Phase 1b safety data in healthy volunteers in late 2024 and aims to launch a Phase 2b trial for major depressive disorder in the first half of 2027. Impact Beyond depression, the capital will support the pipeline's expansion into other neurological and neurodegenerative conditions, such as schizophrenia and Alzheimer's disease. The deal arrives amid renewed industry momentum, highlighted by recent high-profile acquisitions and regulatory focus on psychedelic-based mental health treatments.

item.title: Merck’s MASH drug efinopegdutide succeeds in mid-stage trial
item.description: Clinical Trial Results Merck revealed data from its phase 2b trial involving 386 patients with MASH and stage F2 or F3 fibrosis. Participants received one of three doses of efinopegdutide or a placebo for 52 weeks. The trial met its primary endpoint, showing MASH resolution in 56% to 63% of patients across the different doses, compared to 13% for the placebo arm. Drug Mechanism and Context Efinopegdutide is a subcutaneously injected co-agonist targeting both GLP-1 and glucagon receptors. Merck included a research arm using Novo Nordisk's semaglutide, where 53% achieved MASH resolution. Merck originally licensed the drug from Hanmi Pharmaceutical in 2020 after it passed through Johnson & Johnson's pipeline.

item.title: Cohere Expands Sovereign AI Platform with AISLE and cubic
item.description: According to Cohere Blog: Background and Acquisitions Cohere states that organizations increasingly require AI systems that are powerful, secure, and under their control, a concept the company refers to as sovereign AI. To advance this goal, Cohere has completed its acquisition of AISLE, a builder of autonomous systems for vulnerability discovery and remediation, and welcomed the team behind cubic, an AI-powered code review platform. These transactions mark Cohere's fourth and fifth strategic M&A deals this year, following Aleph Alpha and Reliant AI. Cybersecurity and Prague Hub Following the acquisition, AISLE co-founders are taking key leadership roles: Ondrej Vlcek becomes Senior Vice President of Cohere Cyber, Jaya Baloo becomes Chief Information Security Officer, and Stanislav Fort becomes Vice President of AI Security. Cohere plans a long-term investment in Prague, establishing the city as its global center for AI cybersecurity and autonomous security systems, leveraging AISLE's expertise to build cyber-resilient AI capabilities. Secure Coding and Enterprise Scale Cubic's team, led by founder and CEO Paul Sanglé-Ferrière, brings expertise in AI, security, and developer tools. Their review agents support environments such as on-premises and air-gapped deployments. According to Cohere, this team will establish the company's secure coding vertical, accelerating the integration of enterprise-grade coding and vulnerability remediation capabilities into its platform.

item.title: Regeneron's antibody curbs POTS heart rate spikes in mid-stage trial
item.description: Clinical Trial Results Regeneron reported data from its Phase 2 Pinnacle trial evaluating baloncibart, also known as REGN7544, in 82 patients with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS). Patients receiving a 450-mg injection experienced a mean drop in heart rate of 11.4 beats per minute compared to placebo at day eight, while a 150-mg dose reduced heart rate by 9.5 beats per minute. The high-dose group also showed sustained heart rate reductions and reported improvements in physical functioning at day 29. Mechanism and Development POTS is a chronic autonomic nervous system disorder associated with lightheadedness and fatigue, with no currently approved treatments. Baloncibart is an NPR1-blocking monoclonal antibody designed to increase blood volume in circulation. Regeneron plans to launch a Phase 3 study in the first half of 2027, building on this mid-stage success.

item.title: Robot Talk: Making robots work reliably in high-risk environments
item.description: Real-World Challenges Daniela Shchegelskaya, an engineer from the University of Twente, shares her work on moving autonomous robots from controlled labs into unpredictable real-world settings. She highlights that reliability, connectivity, and system-level design are the biggest hurdles when deploying machines where failure is not an option. Substation Inspections At Elimpus, Shchegelskaya focuses on integrating Boston Dynamics' Spot robot to inspect live power substations. This involves enabling autonomous navigation, remote diagnostics, and data collection in environments with heavy electromagnetic interference and strict safety requirements.

item.title: Biopharma industry looks beyond GLP-1s for next-gen weight loss treatments
item.description: Amylin Pipeline Competition As existing GLP-1 treatments like Wegovy and Zepbound face challenges regarding side effects and plateauing results, amylin analogs are emerging as a primary alternative. Companies such as Novo Nordisk, Eli Lilly, and a partnership between Roche and Zealand Pharma are showcasing data for their pipeline assets, balancing higher efficacy against tolerability trade-offs. Muscle Preservation and Quality Beyond raw weight loss numbers, companies are prioritizing body composition. Biohaven and Wave Life Sciences are presenting data on therapies designed to target myostatin and INHBE proteins, aiming to reduce fat while preserving lean muscle, addressing a major drawback of current incretin drugs. Persistence and Long-Term Value Industry leaders note that roughly half of patients drop out of treatment within six months. Presentations at the conference, including Rhythm Pharmaceuticals' long-term data, highlight the growing importance of treatment durability and persistence in determining the true commercial and clinical value of obesity therapeutics.

item.title: Israel’s VCs see opportunity for challengers in Nvidia’s turmoil
item.description:
Jensen Huang’s resignation has caused anxiety in Israel, where Nvidia employs around 6,000 people and has deep roots following its 2019 acquisition of Mellanox. Local tech figures note that Huang personally drove the company’s heavy investment in the region, raising questions about whether his successor will maintain the same level of commitment. Interim CEO Colette Kress has deep ties to the region, and Israeli executives like Apple’s Johny Srouji and Nvidia’s Michael Kagan have been floated as potential successors.
Despite the local uncertainty, venture capitalists in Israel view the transition as a potential turning point for the broader AI industry. According to Vertex Ventures Israel General Partner Yanai Oron, slower decisions at Nvidia could give rivals an opening, though a broader slowdown in AI spending remains a risk. Selah Ventures founder Adi Levanon notes that while Huang's departure does not dismantle Nvidia's ecosystem, it might prevent the company from becoming a full-on monopoly, giving alternative chip and inference software developers a chance to prove their economic value.

item.title: Nvidia processors power Chinese AI data centre projects worth $3 billion despite US export controls: Report
item.description: Project Details According to a Reuters report, multiple regions in China have incorporated restricted Nvidia processors into their AI infrastructure plans. Projects using H100 and H200 chips span across Fujian, Shaanxi, Jilin, Inner Mongolia, and Gansu provinces, with investments ranging from billions of yuan. Some facilities, such as a computing cluster in Wuxi using H800 processors, are already operational, while institutions like Shenzhen University and Northwestern Polytechnical University have also made smaller chip purchases. Potential Impact The heavy reliance on restricted American technology exposes Chinese developers to significant supply disruptions, construction delays, and rising costs as Washington tightens export controls. Furthermore, developers might eventually be forced to redesign their facilities to accommodate domestically produced alternatives.

item.title: Raise3D Launches T450 and T700 FDM 3D Printers Alongside New Software and Post-Processing Hardware
item.description: Product Launch Details Raise3D has introduced the T450 and large-format T700 FDM 3D printers ahead of Formnext 2026. Both models share a CoreXY motion platform with four frame-mounted motors and TwinFlow high-flow extrusion technology, which feeds two filament paths into a single nozzle. The systems include Air Flow Manager 2 to adjust chamber temperatures up to 70°C, and feature fiber-ready nozzles reaching 420°C. Applications and Pricing According to CEO Edward Feng, the T450's build area enables applications like single-piece adolescent scoliosis braces. Raise3D also reported significant production time and weight reductions for battery cell transport trays. The T450 is priced at $4,999, with deliveries starting in December 2026, while the T700 is priced at $15,999, with deliveries expected by January 2027. Additional Hardware and Software Alongside the new printers, Raise3D announced a 100 mm build-height increase for its RMS220 SLS printer via a software update, and introduced the B520 automated sandblaster for polymer powder bed parts. These developments follow a recent $15 million funding round aimed at supporting product portfolio upgrades and market expansion.

item.title: Nvidia scandal: Howard Lutnick under pressure over alleged lack of action
item.description: 背景与事件起因 据美联社等多家媒体报道，英伟达联合创始人兼CEO黄仁勋于周四辞职，并由首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯担任临时CEO。此前有报道称，黄仁勋卷入多起婚外情，其中包括与涉嫌中国间谍的艾丽斯·黄（Alice Huang）的关系。随着美国情报部门的相关报告在特朗普政府高层流传，舆论风暴迅速升级。 商务部长的压力 批评矛头直指美国商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克。多位国会议员指出，商务部在将与艾丽斯·黄有关联、且曾购买数十亿美元英伟达芯片的新加坡公司Megaspeed列入出口管制黑名单一事上存在拖延行为。白宫官员目前正在讨论是否应将卢特尼克撤职，而他本人已同意在未来几周内出席国会听证会。 行业与政策影响 这起丑闻正值美国收紧对华人工智能芯片出口的关键时刻。多位国会领袖呼吁彻底调查并堵住出口管制漏洞，而中国AI公司正试图在海外寻找替代芯片产能，北京方面也在加速推进以华为为代表的国产芯片替代进程。同时，黄仁勋在中国的巨大影响力和个人崇拜现象也在社交媒体上引发了广泛关注和讨论。

item.title: Oura's acquisition of Counsel Health raises conflict-of-interest concerns for Eli Lilly
item.description:
Smart ring maker Oura announced its acquisition of Counsel Health, a telehealth startup that connects patients with clinicians for popular GLP-1 weight-loss drug prescriptions. Previously, pharmaceutical giant Eli Lilly featured Counsel Health on its curated list of provider options for patients seeking these treatments. Conflict Concerns
According to industry experts, the transaction raises conflict-of-interest questions for Eli Lilly and similar drugmakers. By integrating hardware tracking with direct telehealth diagnosis and prescription services under one corporate umbrella, the acquisition blurs the lines between objective health data collection and commercial treatment pathways, prompting a closer look at how pharmaceutical companies partner with digital health platforms.

item.title: Jensen Huang Steps Down as NVIDIA CEO
item.description:
NVIDIA announced that Jensen Huang has resigned from his positions as president, CEO, and board member after leading the company for 33 years since its founding in 1993. Following the announcement, the company's stock experienced a significant drop in pre-market trading before recovering slightly.
Executive Vice President and CFO Colette Kress has been named interim CEO while maintaining her current financial responsibilities. Kress has been with NVIDIA for over 13 years and previously held financial leadership roles at Cisco and Microsoft. Additionally, the board appointed Harvey C. Jones as NVIDIA's first-ever board chairman. The company confirmed that its Q3 fiscal 2027 earnings will be released on November 17 as originally scheduled.

item.title: ESA clarifies Prometheus engine tests are separate from Themis rocket delays
item.description: Engine Testing Update ArianeGroup announced that a series of hot-fire tests for the latest Prometheus rocket engine were completed on October 29 at DLR's P5 test bench in Lampoldshausen. According to the company, these tests were carried out independently of preparations for the Themis reusable booster demonstrator. A primary goal of this late-October campaign was to validate a new combustion chamber produced through a Cold Gas Spray additive manufacturing process, which aims to reduce production time and costs. Themis Flight Delays Meanwhile, the inaugural flight of the Themis reusable booster remains significantly delayed. Although officials previously targeted early 2026 for the first hop test from the Esrange Space Centre in Sweden, the vehicle remains grounded as winter approaches. During an October press conference, ESA's Director of Space Transportation stated that operators would decide by late November whether a 2026 inaugural flight is still feasible before winter weather halts testing.

item.title: US Lawmakers Summon Ex-Nvidia CEO After Spy Scandal
item.description:
Following the resignation of Nvidia's long-time leader after reports of extramarital affairs, US lawmakers have moved quickly to demand answers. Republican Senator Tim Scott requested that the former CEO and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick testify before the Senate Banking Committee in December, while three House committees also called for a closed-door interview.
Reports allege that one of the individuals involved was an asset of China's Ministry of State Security, raising serious concerns regarding the protection of sensitive US technology. The unfolding situation has wiped almost half a trillion dollars off Nvidia's market valuation, thrown the company into leadership transition with CFO Colette Kress serving as interim CEO, and left the broader AI industry navigating uncharted political and security waters.

item.title: Zugwise: Domain-Aware Game Reconstruction for Digitizing Handwritten Chess Scoresheets
item.description: The authors report in this preprint: Digitizing handwritten chess scoresheets has traditionally been framed as a handwriting-recognition task combined with move legality checks. However, the authors argue that this misses silent errors where a misread yields a legal but incorrect move, corrupting the remainder of the game. To address this, the authors present Zugwise, which repurposes computer-chess machinery—such as quiescence search, static exchange evaluation, and pin detection—to evaluate whether a human could have plausibly written a given sequence. It incorporates an absurdity detector, backward search for tracing error symptoms, and a Needleman-Wunsch merge combining evidence from both players' sheets. Evaluated on tournament sections in an oracle replay, the system reduced silent errors from 16 to 1 and from 50 to 13. Two learned signals (CTC re-scoring and a Maia-style human-move prior) raised the correct fix's top-rank rate from 58.8% to 78.0%. The software runs entirely in the browser and is free, private, and offline-capable, accompanied by a three-way adjudication protocol.

item.title: Abstention Is Not Threshold Compliance: Stated Scoring Rules in Open Language Models
item.description: The authors report in this preprint: This paper investigates the proposal by Kalai et al. to use explicit probability thresholds in prompts as scoring rules, directing language models to answer only when their confidence exceeds threshold t. The authors probe 12 checkpoints across three post-training stages from four open 3-8B model recipes, alongside exploratory models up to 32B. The empirical tests reveal that while a strict abstention format line shifts mean abstention from 20% to 91% at t = 0.75, varying t from 0.5 to 0.9 within this format changes abstention by a mere -0.8 percentage points. Without formatting prompts, higher thresholds can paradoxically lower abstention, with up to 40% of items receiving decisions incompatible with threshold-independent beliefs. Furthermore, external thresholds on recalibrated P(True) showed brittle generalization across datasets like TriviaQA and PopQA, and models trained on threshold-conditioned targets failed to track unseen thresholds consistently. The study concludes that high abstention rates do not imply true rule compliance and outlines rigorous evaluation criteria for stated scoring rules.

item.title: Robust AI builds collaborative mobile robots for warehouses and factories
item.description: According to MIT Robotics: Background and Origins Robust AI was co-founded in 2019 by Anthony Jules and MIT Professor Emeritus Rodney Brooks, known for his work leading CSAIL and co-founding iRobot and Rethink Robotics. After navigating early pivots prompted by the Covid-19 pandemic, the founders leveraged years of customer interviews to focus on logistics and manufacturing industries that lack full automation. Technology and Workflows The company's flagship mobile robot, Carter, resembles a utility cart and is built for fast-changing warehouse environments. It features a force-sensitive handlebar, holonomic wheels, and an AI-powered vision system, allowing humans to easily guide, push, pull, or direct it using gestures. Carter is designed to phase into operations as needed, handling tasks like moving items across large facilities where human workers might otherwise walk up to 30,000 steps a day. Human-Robot Interaction Robust AI emphasizes human agency, drawing lessons from past automation failures where rigid robots blocked hospital corridors. By designing the digital system to support rather than disrupt human workflows, the company aims to let humans do what they do best while letting machines handle repetitive physical transport.

item.title: AI Recording Gadgets Are Living on Borrowed Time as Tech Giants Move In
item.description: The Shift in Recording Hardware Standalone AI recording cards like Plaud have enjoyed massive success since 2023, but the core function of recording and transcribing is easily matched by phones and apps. To survive, newer devices are shifting focus from professional meetings to capturing a user's entire day to build personal AI contexts. The Phone Maker Advantage Tech giants are quickly closing this gap. Apple added live dialogue rewind and daily recaps to the Apple Watch, while domestic brands like OPPO and Alibaba are launching devices that instantly discard raw audio after cloud transcription, keeping only the text. However, third-party hardware still faces friction because major apps block direct AI control, making standalone or wearable mics a necessary workaround to capture offline conversations. The Race for the Agent Gateway Ultimately, these collected contexts are read by AI agents rather than humans. As phone makers race to integrate system-level memory engines by mid-2027, standalone hardware faces a tight six-month window to position itself as a practical peripheral before users rely entirely on built-in phone capabilities.

item.title: Building strong safety evaluations
item.description:
According to Anthropic Research: Background and Challenges
Safety evaluations guide critical decisions regarding AI model deployment and safeguards. However, researchers have found that AI evals are easily gamed, poorly documented, and sensitive to minor formatting changes. Drawing on psychological research reforms, Anthropic outlines best practices for building trustworthy safety evaluations. Design and Execution Best Practices
Building strong evaluations requires matching the design to the core question, whether observational or causal, and measuring the right construct, such as appropriate response rates instead of simple refusal rates in sensitive contexts like self-harm or dual-use biology. Evals should use multi-turn simulations to capture nuanced, escalating user behavior and run in secure, sandboxed environments to prevent unintended actions. Grader Validation and Reporting
Since modern evaluations rely on AI graders, teams must calibrate them rigorously, ensure atomic and binary criteria, and validate them against human labels. Furthermore, researchers should preregister analysis plans, report full statistics with confidence intervals, and disclose model configurations transparently to ensure results are reproducible.

item.title: The patient in the conversation: why biomedical engineering needs a reality check
item.description: The Patient Perspective in Research Editors at Nature Biomedical Engineering emphasize that while submitted studies often feature impressive novelty and technical rigor, a common flaw is the lack of a compelling clinical need. Through an example of engineered bacteria targeting tumors that required prior metabolic labelling of cancer cells, editors illustrate how lab success often ignores the messy realities of patient care, such as administration routes, safety, and scalability. Practical Challenges Across Fields This patient-centric lens applies widely. In regenerative medicine, complex manufacturing and cold-chain storage hinder adoption. In medical devices, ingestible tools that require surgical retrieval fall short compared to those that naturally dissolve or excrete. For biomedical AI, hurdles involve data privacy and systemic bottlenecks rather than just model performance. Simplified, cost-effective, and side-effect-reducing technologies are crucial for broad accessibility. A Call for Early Realism The goal is not to discourage basic research, but to encourage translational researchers to anticipate clinical barriers right from the design stage. By evaluating whether benefits justify complexity, researchers can ensure their innovations genuinely improve patient lives.

item.title: A unified and practical taxonomy for false discovery rate control in omics research
item.description: Background In fields like genomics and mass spectrometry, researchers test thousands of biological features at once, creating a massive risk of false positives. While many statistical procedures exist to control the false discovery rate, they rely on different assumptions, making it confusing for scientists to choose the right one. Details and Impact To solve this, the authors propose a practical taxonomy organized around a 2 × 2 matrix. According to the authors, this matrix is designed to guide researchers in sequencing-based and mass-spectrometry-based omics. It helps them select either the most appropriate family of false discovery rate procedures or alternative, more rigorous methods tailored to their specific experimental setup.

item.title: Zura scraps hidradenitis suppurativa drug program after clinical trial failure
item.description:
Zura Bio reported that its drug tibulizumab failed in a phase 2 trial involving 247 patients with hidradenitis suppurativa (HS), a chronic inflammatory skin condition. The study compared two doses of the drug against a placebo, but the trial missed its primary endpoint because patients taking the placebo showed similar improvement rates in reducing abscesses and nodules compared to those taking the medication. Although the drug's actual response rates were comparable to another approved treatment on the market, the unusually high effectiveness in the placebo arm doomed the trial.
In response to the clinical setback, investors sent Zura's stock down 72% to $1.12 when markets opened. Despite dropping the HS indication, Zura CEO Sandeep Kulkarni noted that the company will continue testing the asset in other conditions like systemic sclerosis and polymyalgia rheumatica, which have completely different disease mechanisms. Furthermore, Zura reported that the drug was generally well-tolerated with manageable safety results, and the company ended September with $187.7 million in cash, providing a financial runway through at least the end of 2028.

item.title: Spruce spins off preclinical endocrinology program into Adrenyx with up to $50 million backing
item.description:
According to a Nov. 9 release, Spruce Biosciences is creating a subsidiary named Adrenyx Biosciences to house its preclinical endocrinology program, specifically the monoclonal antibody CRHX-101 (formerly SPR-202) for congenital adrenal hyperplasia.
The transaction structure involves an initial $5 million promissory note from an unnamed institutional biotechnology investor, with a total commitment of up to $50 million. The companies plan to operate as separate, publicly traded entities led by Spruce CFO Samir Gharib, pending regulatory and listing approvals in the first half of next year.
Strategic focus enables Spruce to concentrate resources on its lead neurological candidate TA-ERT for Sanfilippo syndrome type B, following a period of workforce reductions and manufacturing data delays.

item.title: Boehringer plans 2027 survodutide submission after positive heart safety trial
item.description:
Boehringer Ingelheim presented results from the Synchronize-CVOT study at the American Heart Association Scientific Sessions, showing that survodutide achieved a hazard ratio of 0.89 in comparing major adverse cardiovascular events against placebo among 5,530 adult participants. The dual glucagon and GLP-1 receptor agonist also met secondary endpoints regarding cardiometabolic health markers.
While the drug demonstrated a meaningful weight loss of up to 13.7% at Week 72, it faces intense competition from established blockbusters like Eli Lilly's Zepbound. Furthermore, the trial noted higher discontinuation rates due to gastrointestinal adverse events, ranging between 19.3% and 20.8% across treatment arms, though company representatives express confidence that flexible dosing adjustments in future practice will mitigate this issue.
Boehringer is pursuing a dual-path regulatory strategy, aiming to seek approval for both obesity and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), with the initial weight loss application targeted for submission next year.

item.title: Google Announces 'Gemini 4 Hydrogen', a Fast and Low-Cost Model Available to Free Users
item.description: Background and Positioning Google has introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen as the third model in the Gemini 4 series, following Argon and Carbon. Google positions Hydrogen as its mainstream model for daily agent tasks, emphasizing speed and efficiency. Performance and Comparisons According to Artificial Analysis, Hydrogen scores 51 points on standard reasoning, outperforming Argon. Google reports it is about 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash. In Google's benchmark comparisons against Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 5.5 and OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Terra, Hydrogen led in 7 out of 10 items, including the HLE-Diamond reasoning test at 58.8%, while trailing in terminal operations and computer use. Pricing and Availability Hydrogen features a 1-million-token context window. API pricing is set at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per output token. It is available immediately across multiple developer platforms, Google Workspace tools, and the free tier of the Gemini app.

item.title: MIT researchers tackle space nuclear power and radiation detection challenges
item.description: According to MIT Energy: Thermal management in space As deep space missions demand higher power, nuclear reactors produce significant heat. Without an atmosphere for convection, traditional solid metal radiators are too heavy. According to MIT, Hecla is investigating the liquid droplet radiator (LDR), which uses sheets of tiny droplets to radiate heat away, potentially reducing cooling system mass by an order of magnitude. Radiation detection and Chernobyl Hecla’s passion for radiation detection began in childhood and led him to research X-ray units and treaty verification methods at MIT. His experiences visiting Chernobyl shaped his commitment to nuclear safety and radioactive contamination management, eventually influencing his graduate research on radiation imaging and antineutrino detection. Safeguards and space security Hecla’s research extends to monitoring aerospace nuclear applications, such as tracking air-breathing nuclear propulsion and detecting fissile material from satellites. By developing compact neutron telescopes and tracking operational signatures, his work aims to create a technical foundation for future arms-control agreements.

item.title: Deploy frontier AI models on AWS Trainium with SGLang-Neuron
item.description: According to AWS Machine Learning: Background Amazon announced that SGLang-Neuron is now publicly available through an AWS Deep Learning Container. Built by RadixArk in collaboration with Annapurna Labs, the tool brings SGLang's popular serving framework to AWS Trainium, Amazon's proprietary AI chip portfolio designed for cost-effective training and inference at scale. Technical Details SGLang-Neuron operates as an out-of-tree plugin that connects SGLang with AWS Trainium. The core SGLang framework handles the API server, request management, and RadixAttention, while the plugin manages Trainium-specific models, attention mechanisms, Mixture of Experts (MoE), and graph execution using native PyTorch and the Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI). It also supports PD disaggregation, allowing prefill and decode phases to run on separate servers and transfer KV caches via Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA). Practical Impact Developers can now deploy models on Trainium using the exact same SGLang APIs and server interfaces they already use. This lowers the barrier to adopting AWS hardware for large-scale model serving and reinforcement learning workloads without requiring a complete rewrite of their serving pipelines.

item.title: Bill Gates-backed Breakthrough Energy says global decarbonization would cost 7.5 trillion dollars
item.description: According to MIT Climate: Background and Costs Eric Toone, chief technical officer at Breakthrough Energy, spoke at MIT's annual energy conference, highlighting that rising global prosperity inherently drives up energy demand and greenhouse gas emissions. According to Toone, while decarbonizing the world economy is entirely feasible, the true challenge lies not just in the calculated 7.5 trillion dollar cost, but in the reality that consumers and even wealthy individuals are largely unwilling to pay extra for zero-carbon alternatives. By enlisting artificial intelligence, the organization estimated this multi-trillion-dollar price tag, which could potentially drop to 3.5 trillion dollars if emerging technologies succeed. Technology Solutions Breakthrough Energy Ventures has deployed approximately 3 billion dollars into roughly 140 companies tackling clean energy challenges. Noteworthy examples include Luxwall, which produces highly insulating windows capable of cutting commercial building energy use by 30 percent, and Form Energy, which is developing iron-air batteries designed to store power for up to a month. Other portfolio companies are addressing cement emissions, upgrading transmission lines, advancing geothermal drilling through adapted fracking technology, and creating magnetic containment solutions for fusion energy. Industry Impact Toone noted that while Breakthrough's investments are substantial, they represent only a fraction of broader global clean tech funding. The ultimate hurdle facing the energy transition is the sheer scale of existing infrastructure that must be replaced, making it critical to deploy these innovative technologies directly into emerging and developing economies to prevent future carbon-heavy infrastructure buildouts.

item.title: AI-related stocks send Taiwanese investors into a frenzy
item.description: Background In Taiwan, taxi drivers and everyday citizens are increasingly fixated on the stock market every morning as trading begins in Taipei. Although their daily jobs have no connection to high finance, many keep a watchful eye on the performance of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company to safeguard their personal savings and future. Core Details Local residents often refer to the company as the sacred mountain that protects the country, a sentiment that has intensified with the massive adoption of artificial intelligence. While companies like Nvidia design advanced AI processors in California, the actual physical production relies entirely on TSMC's manufacturing facilities on Taiwan's west coast. Market Impact Having long been essential for producing popular consumer tech products like Apple's iPhone processors, the sudden explosion of the artificial intelligence sector has pushed the company to unprecedented heights. Its market capitalization has surged dramatically over a three-year period, establishing it as a dominant economic force outside the United States.

item.title: LLMON: An LLM-Native Markup Language, now in Granite 4.1 3B and 8B
item.description: Background and Motivation Large language models rely heavily on context to generate tokens, but traditional formats like JSON were designed for parsers rather than causal models. Because transformers struggle with long spans and statistical quotation matching, models can become brittle or vulnerable to attacks such as prompt injections. To fix this, developers created LLMON (LLM Object Notation), which uses an XML-like structure with reserved special tokens to cleanly separate instructions, data, and requirements. Implementation and Capabilities Today, experimental preview models derived from Granite 4.1 base models, specifically granite-4.1-3b-LLMON-preview and granite-4.1-8b-LLMON-preview, have been released alongside a GitHub toolkit. Unlike regular chat templates that flatten inputs into a single string, LLMON wraps semantically coherent components in meaningful tags and uses an execution block to bind specific instructions to their exact data payloads. Evaluated on the OPI benchmark, these models virtually eliminate static indirect prompt injections, showing significantly higher robustness compared to standard open-source and closed-source models while matching general capabilities.

item.title: Cardiovascular Drug Development Faces Major Setbacks and Upcoming Milestones
item.description:
BioSpace reports on a turbulent period for cardiovascular drug development, highlighted by a series of late-stage clinical trial failures. According to Oppenheimer analysts, the sector experienced six clinical failures within nine weeks. Notable setbacks include Novo Nordisk's IL-6 inhibitor ziltivekimab, which failed to reduce cardiovascular risks, and Novartis's antisense therapy pelacarsen, which lowered Lp(a) levels without generating clinical benefit. Additionally, AstraZeneca and Ionis Pharmaceuticals reported a disappointing Phase 3 result for their TTR silencer Wainua.
Despite these challenges, the sector has seen positive developments. The FDA approved Eli Lilly's Mounjaro to lower cardiovascular risks in type 2 diabetes patients, and Merck secured approval for an oral PCSK9 inhibitor. Furthermore, early-stage trials showed promising results for Verve's base editor VERVE-102 in lowering LDL cholesterol.
Looking ahead, the fourth quarter brings critical readouts. NewAmsterdam Pharma anticipates Phase 3 data for its CETP inhibitor obicetrapib, while Johnson & Johnson and Bristol Myers Squibb await results from a Phase 3 trial of the oral Factor XIa inhibitor milvexian for secondary stroke prevention.

item.title: 1.15.41 - Software release featuring private URL security updates and dependency fixes
item.description:
Detailed Features
Vidit-Ostwal reports the release of version 1.15.41. The update introduces a new feature that allows approved private URL hosts, enhancing how external links and internal resources are managed within the software. Bug Fixes and Improvements
The authors state several important bug fixes in this release. Projects are updated to depend on PyMuPDF 2.x. Additionally, a real storage URL has been removed from the URL read tests, and the LiteLLM path now properly strips the cache_breakpoint marker. The system also retains earlier step outputs during a human-feedback resume process.

item.title: Google Introduces Gemini 4 Hydrogen Model for Fast Execution and Agentic Workflows
item.description: According to Google DeepMind: Background and Positioning Google is rolling out Gemini 4 Hydrogen to bring cutting-edge intelligence and speed to everyday coding and agentic workflows. While frontier models like Carbon and Argon handle deep, long-horizon reasoning on complex problems, Hydrogen is built as an efficient execution engine for rapid tasks and multi-model collaboration. Performance and Features According to Google, Hydrogen surpasses Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high-thinking level. It features a 1-million-token context window with flat pricing of $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens. In developer benchmarks, it triples its predecessor's Terminal-Bench scores and significantly reduces hallucinated claims. The model supports four adjustable thinking levels to balance quality, latency, and cost. Ecosystem Integration Hydrogen is rolling out globally across the Gemini API, Google AI Studio, the Gemini app, Google Search, and enterprise tools. Google is also introducing Orchestrator in Google Antigravity, a feature that dynamically switches between models like Carbon and Hydrogen within a single session to optimize task success rates while reducing token quota consumption.

item.title: Google Search Gets Major Upgrade with Gemini 4 Hydrogen
item.description:
According to Google AI:
Google reports that Gemini 4 Hydrogen is now available globally for all users in Google Search, representing its largest model upgrade for the search engine so far. Key Improvements According to Google, the upgrade features better understanding of intent, allowing Search to handle multi-part questions, typos, and specific requests. It also uses advanced reasoning to improve query fan-out and linking, simultaneously searching subtopics to surface a wider range of relevant websites. Visual and Language Experience Users will see more visual responses, including images, structured layouts, comparison tables, and custom tools. Additionally, the system provides richer language understanding across all supported AI Mode languages.

item.title: Stratasys and Nano Dimension call off MarkForged acquisition
item.description: Background Earlier this year, Stratasys and Nano Dimension agreed to an all-cash transaction worth 42.5 million USD that would allow Stratasys to acquire MarkForged from Nano Dimension. Details According to Stratasys, the original plan was subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals expected by the end of the year. However, by November, both parties concluded that these regulatory hurdles were unlikely to be cleared by the start of 2027. Under the original deal, Stratasys was set to purchase MarkForged's polymer, composite, and metal extrusion portfolio, while Nano Dimension would retain the metal binder jetting line that MarkForged previously acquired from Digital Metal. Impact Stratasys stated that the termination does not change the strength or direction of its standalone business, allowing the company to move forward with greater focus and flexibility. Meanwhile, with Nano Dimension exploring pivots away from the additive manufacturing industry, the future of MarkForged remains unclear.

item.title: US AI Data Centers Face Resistance from Local Politics and Community Opposition
item.description: Policy and Community Pressures on Infrastructure As US AI infrastructure investments scale up, data center projects are encountering unexpected hurdles from local zoning boards, state politics, and community opposition. Industry experts note that local residents in regions like Texas and California are increasingly pushing back against massive power and water consumption, raising concerns about utility costs and long-term community benefits. These local friction points, ranging from environmental permits to grid interconnection bottlenecks, threaten to increase project costs by 10% to 20% and cause widespread construction delays. Market Dynamics and Supply Chain Vulnerabilities Wall Street's recent sell-off in AI-related stocks reflects growing anxiety over the sustainability of massive capital expenditures and circular financing structures. Panelists discussed the potential mismatch between hardware supply and actual software demand, raising questions about whether data center slowdowns could create shortages in specific components while leaving upstream chip capacity vulnerable if token economics or model efficiency shift.

item.title: Blackstone backs Pfizer's monthly obesity treatment, while FDA nominee faces a tight vote
item.description: Blackstone is providing financial backing for Pfizer's development of a monthly obesity treatment. In regulatory news, the Senate health committee is scheduled to vote next Wednesday on Heidi Overton’s nomination to lead the FDA. Committee Chair Bill Cassidy remains undecided, describing her past role in shaping the Trump administration's vaccine policies as nearly disqualifying. Given the political split, a single Republican defection could block the nomination if all Democrats vote against her. Additionally, drugmaker Bristol Myers Squibb has restructured its research and development organization. Current Chief Medical Officer Cristian Massacesi has assumed the additional role of head of R&D, while Robert Plenge, the current chief of research, will step down in March. Separately, Reuters reports that the FDA has shelved its Commissioner’s National Priority Voucher program.

item.title: Neurosterix raises $105 million to advance schizophrenia drug
item.description: Funding and Leadership Neurosterix announced a $105 million Series B financing led by RTW Investments, with participation from GV and Janus Henderson Investors. The company also recruited three former Karuna Therapeutics leaders, appointing Andrew Miller as executive chair, Edmund Harrigan as an independent director, and Stephen Brannan as chair of the clinical advisory board. Drug Development Strategy The new capital will primarily fund mid-stage trials for NTX-253, an oral muscarinic M4 positive allosteric modulator designed to treat schizophrenia. The company aims to fine-tune brain signaling to reduce psychosis symptoms while avoiding the movement and metabolic side effects typical of traditional dopamine antagonists. Market Context The muscarinic receptor space has gained significant attention following Bristol Myers Squibb's approval of Cobenfy and its $14 billion acquisition of Karuna. Meanwhile, other competitors like AbbVie faced setbacks when their M4 candidate emraclidine failed mid-stage trials.

item.title: Sanofi-backed Windward aims for $204M IPO to fund respiratory drugs
item.description: IPO Details and Financials Swiss biotech Windward Bio has filed for a Nasdaq IPO, offering 10.3 million shares priced between $16 and $18 each. According to its regulatory filing, the company expects to raise approximately $203.8 million in net proceeds, which could increase to $228 million if underwriters exercise their full options. Core Pipeline and Chinese Assets The primary focus of the IPO proceeds is WIN378, an anti-TSLP monoclonal antibody acquired from Kelun-Biotech and Harbour BioMed in a $970 million deal. Windward plans to use up to $227.5 million to complete ongoing phase 2 studies in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and asthma, alongside an upcoming phase 3 trial. Additionally, the company is developing WIN027, a dual-targeting antibody licensed from Qyuns Therapeutics, with funds allocated for a phase 2b COPD study and an atopic dermatitis trial. Investor Support and Market Context Windward is led by CEO Luca Santarelli and has a history of strong financial backing, including a $200 million series A and a $165 million series B round. Alongside the public offering, Sanofi has agreed to purchase $50 million of Windward's stock in a private placement, underscoring major industry interest in anti-TSLP therapies for immunological and respiratory conditions.

item.title: Jaya Baloo Joins Cohere as First CISO
item.description:
According to Cohere Blog:
Cohere announces the appointment of Jaya Baloo as its first Chief Information Security Officer (CISO). Baloo brings over two decades of cybersecurity experience, having previously served as CISO at Rapid7, Avast, and KPN Telecom, and as co-founder of AI-native cybersecurity startup AISLE.
As enterprise adoption shifts from pilot projects to production, organizations—particularly governments and critical infrastructure operators—are demanding higher standards of security, governance, and control. Cohere states that Baloo's expertise in critical infrastructure security and quantum readiness will guide the company's strategy in delivering secure deployment infrastructure and frontier AI models.

item.title: Ask Me Anything: The Verge reviews Apple's first smart display, HomeView
item.description: Jen Tuohy, a senior smart home reviewer at The Verge, has tested Apple's newly released $299 HomeView smart display. Over the past week, she tried both the tabletop and wall-mounted versions across different rooms, including the kitchen, bedroom, office, and entryway, testing its cooking assistance, smart home controls, calling features, and new Siri AI capabilities. She also observed how different family members interacted with the device. Verge subscribers can now submit questions in the comments section, with the live answering session scheduled to begin at 2 PM ET.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns following personal scandals
item.description:
Jensen Huang, the 63-year-old founder and CEO of Nvidia, has stepped down from his role after a series of personal revelations. On Sunday, November 8, Huang admitted to having a relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese entrepreneur suspected by US intelligence agencies of spying for Beijing. Shortly after, on Wednesday, November 11, news emerged of a second romantic relationship with a subordinate who is an executive at Nvidia.
In response to these developments, Nvidia's board of directors convened urgently on Wednesday evening and announced his resignation on Thursday. Huang, who led the company since its founding in 1993, had previously shifted its focus toward artificial intelligence and ruled the organization with direct management over roughly 60 reports. He had not established a succession plan, leaving the tech giant suddenly without its long-time leader.

item.title: Chinese Workers Are Paying Their Own AI Bills to Stay Productive
item.description: Background and Survey Data Survey data indicate that generative AI users in China will exceed 700 million by mid-2026, with about a third using the tools for work. Research shows that more than a third of respondents pay for large-model access, and nearly three in ten buy dedicated AI office products. Outside a few tech giants, corporate reimbursement remains rare, leaving individuals, students, and early-career researchers to cover the shortfalls. Spending and Use Cases Workers use paid AI tools across four main clusters: drafting and slides, meeting notes and translation, data cleaning and light coding, and specialized work like contract review. Costs vary by user needs, ranging from a few hundred yuan a month for journalists to around 3,000 yuan for fund managers who rely on AI for research code. E-commerce platforms and telecom operators now offer token recharges alongside ordinary consumer goods, turning AI usage into a regular household bill. Cost Factors and Future Outlook Pricing design opacity and token-based metering drive up monthly expenses, as users often stack multiple subscriptions and burn credits on prompt tuning. Until employers treat AI access as standard infrastructure or vendors make pricing more transparent, workers will continue to subsidize the efficiency expected by their employers.

item.title: BMS R&D Head to Depart Amid Major Restructure
item.description: Restructure Details Bristol Myers Squibb announced a major reorganization to merge its early research and clinical development into a single organization, effective at the start of next year. Robert Plenge, the Chief Research Officer, is set to leave his role by the end of the year and transition to an advisory capacity through March 2027. Cristian Massacesi, currently the Chief Medical Officer and development head, will lead the new unified R&D division. Pipeline Pressures According to the company, the move is designed to accelerate pipeline development and better integrate new technology. BMS is under mounting pressure as two of its blockbuster drugs, Eliquis and Opdivo, approach patent cliffs. Together, these two medications accounted for roughly half of the company's $48.2 billion total revenue, leaving analysts concerned about the risk profile of upcoming pipeline replacements like Cobenfy and milvexian.

item.title: Zimbabwean Author Cleared of Using AI for Award-Winning Story
item.description: Investigation Details Simbarashe Kundizeza won the £10,000 Caine Prize for his short story *The Blue Fighter*. Shortly after, *The Atlantic* published an article suggesting the story was artificially generated, citing the Pangram detection tool. Resolution and Impact In response, the prize organizers conducted a thorough review, including interviews and metadata analysis of drafts. Chair Ellah Wakatama confirmed the story is human-written. The incident also sparked online outrage regarding whether minority writers face unfair algorithmic scrutiny.

item.title: AMD Announces Instinct MI430X GPU with Native FP64 and HBM4 Memory
item.description: According to AMD Blogs: Hardware Architecture and Specifications AMD reports that the Instinct MI430X GPU is designed for the convergence of high-precision scientific computing and AI workloads. Built on the CDNA 5 architecture, it delivers up to 288 TFLOPS of peak native FP64 performance alongside 432 GB of HBM4 memory running at 23.3 TB/s bandwidth. For multi-GPU scaling, a node pairs a 6th Gen EPYC server CPU with four GPUs using a fully connected, switchless Infinity Fabric mesh. Research on FP64 Emulation Limits In a paper presented at SC26, AMD researchers evaluated the limits of Ozaki GEMM emulation on HPC systems. Their analysis suggests that less than 10% of the broader HPC ecosystem features workloads dense and GEMM-shaped enough to benefit from emulation, indicating that native double precision remains essential for stencils, sparse linear algebra, and molecular dynamics. System Deployments and Projections AMD states that the MI430X has been selected for several prominent European and US scientific systems, including Discovery at Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Alice Recoque in France, and Herder in Germany. Performance figures provided by AMD are projected estimates based on engineering benchmarks comparing the MI430X to the previous-generation MI300A APU.

item.title: Can we finally fix growing drug shortages?
item.description: Background In this episode of the Denatured podcast, BioSpace Director of Insights Jennifer C. Smith-Parker talks with Antheia CEO Christina Smolke and Cencora data and AI product head Kyle Pudenz about the rising threat of drug shortages. Details and Approach The discussion examines the root causes behind worsening medicine shortages. The guests explore potential solutions, focusing on how predictive supply-chain analytics can anticipate disruptions and how agile, distributed manufacturing can make the production of essential medicines more resilient and accessible to patients.

item.title: Meta Signs Clean Manufacturing Agreements for Data Center Supply Chains
item.description: According to Meta Newsroom AI: Background Meta reports that it is taking steps to green its data center supply chains by targeting upstream manufacturing processes. Details According to Meta, the company has entered into long-term purchase agreements with various low-carbon producers across its supply chain network. Impact Meta states that these agreements are designed to bring clean manufacturing directly to its data center operations and help set an industry standard for low-carbon supply chain practices.

item.title: D-Wave Named a Market Shaper in Gartner Quantum Computing Report
item.description:
According to D-Wave News:
D-Wave Quantum Inc. announced it has been recognized as a Market Shaper in the Gartner Emerging Market Quadrant for Quantum Computing - Established Vendors as of November 2026, placing among six vendors in the upper right quadrant. Gartner defines Market Shapers as organizations building solutions capable of fundamentally replacing classical computing bottlenecks rather than simply augmenting existing workflows, delivering scalable fault-tolerant architectures and high-fidelity logical qubits.
D-Wave CEO Dr. Alan Baratz stated that the recognition reflects the transformative potential of the company's technology and its execution capabilities. D-Wave provides both quantum annealing and gate-model systems, software, and services, offering enterprise customers access to its Leap quantum cloud service and on-premises systems.

item.title: MiniMax Open-Sources H3-Image Model with Native 4K and Advanced Reasoning
item.description: Background MiniMax, known for its focus on multimodal AI development, has followed up on its video model releases by introducing H3-Image, a new SOTA-level image generation model designed to tackle both aesthetic quality and logical reasoning in visual tasks. Capabilities and Performance According to tests and company reports, H3-Image significantly reduces the artificial appearance common in AI-generated images, successfully rendering human skin textures, realistic lighting, and complex reflections. Beyond aesthetics, the model demonstrates strong spatial awareness and reasoning. It can generate standard orthographic three-view drawings from reference photos, create mechanical explosion diagrams with assembly logic, and accurately typeset and solve complex academic content such as calculus exams. Ecosystem and Impact Supporting up to 16 reference images for character and style consistency, H3-Image delivers native 4K resolution (16MP) with generation speeds under 20 seconds. By offering the model as open-source alongside competitively priced API access, MiniMax aims to lower the barrier for commercial applications ranging from industrial design and gaming concepts to marketing materials.

item.title: Biogen faces a major test with upcoming Phase 3 lupus trial results
item.description: Biogen is approaching a pivotal moment as it anticipates data from the TOPAZ-1 and TOPAZ-2 Phase 3 clinical trials evaluating the drug litifilimab for lupus, scheduled for the first half of December. According to STAT reporter Adam Feuerstein, this upcoming readout represents more than just a standard drug evaluation. Strategic Stakes The impending results serve as a major test for the R&D revamp and growth strategy implemented by CEO Chris Viehbacher since taking the helm in 2022. Because the company previously experienced a positive Phase 3 outcome with another lupus drug called dapirolizumab over two years ago, expectations and risks are both running high for this new portfolio readout.

item.title: Alnylam faces pressure to solve its heart drug challenges
item.description: In his newsletter column, biotech writer Adam Feuerstein reflects on a previous comparison between Alnylam and Vertex from August 2025. While Alnylam showed rapid growth driven by its cardiomyopathy treatment Amvuttra, aiming for a market value comparable to Vertex's $100 billion, Feuerstein points out that the company now faces critical hurdles. Specifically, Alnylam needs to navigate its heart drug issues to justify its ambitious valuation and maintain investor confidence in a competitive biotech market.

item.title: AM Solutions launches D3 post-processing system for EOS P 770 additive manufacturing platform
item.description: System Design and Workflow According to AM Solutions, the D3 system is divided into three sequential stations within a fully enclosed setup. After a build job cools, an actuator moves the parts and powder into a chamber for vibration processing, followed by powder screening into Polyboxes. The process takes approximately 20 minutes for a PA 12 build job. The system avoids compressed air, using the surrounding powder as a protective cushion to prevent friction and impact damage during cleaning. Powder Management and Recovery Project Manager Alexander Gückel notes that the D3 features an optional 'Unpacking Plus' function, which enables powder recovery rates of up to 95 percent. This function also separates thermally less-stressed powder from the peripheral zones of the build job from the heavily stressed powder near the parts, allowing operators to selectively return peripheral powder to the powder loop. Industry Context and Beta Testing The D3 is currently undergoing beta testing at FKM Additive Manufacturing. Managing Director Matthias Henkel states that the automation helps reduce manual work and employee exposure to polymer powder. Vanessa Seidenschwarz, Head of Product and Program Management Polymer at EOS, adds that the system contributes to scalable additive manufacturing for large-format production. The D3 is scheduled to premiere live at Formnext 2026.

item.title: Max Jaderberg on Isomorphic Labs' Vision for AI-Driven Drug Discovery
item.description:
Isomorphic Labs president Max Jaderberg spoke with Elad Gil about the company's approach to transforming drug discovery from empirical trial and error into a computational discipline. Jaderberg noted that traditional drug development is slow and costly, and argued that success with models like AlphaFold demonstrates how deep learning can generalize in biology. He explained that Isomorphic focuses on building disease-agnostic drug design engines capable of handling various target classes and modalities.
According to Jaderberg, scaling AI models allows them to compound learnings and achieve generalizability, which could increase the probability of success in real-world clinical trials. He shared his perspective that accurate molecular engineering may eventually reduce the reliance on animal testing through in-silico models and could enable sophisticated multidrug cocktails targeting complex biological pathways. Jaderberg also discussed the long-term outlook for treating diseases and improving human healthspan as computational optimization advances.

item.title: ESA Explains Delay in Signing MaiaSpace Launcher Challenge Contract
item.description: Background During the 2025 Ministerial Council meeting, member states committed €902.16 million to the European Launcher Challenge, a program designed to support commercial rocket developers.
